section_summary.extract_value: This Introduction section establishes the theoretical framework for a study examining body appreciation as a central construct in understanding positive body image. The authors argue that positive body image is distinct from simply low levels of negative body image, and they present a model incorporating interpersonal variables (restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages, attachment insecurity) and intrapersonal variables (maladaptive and adaptive perfectionism) as predictors of body appreciation, with depressive symptoms and intuitive eating as outcomes. The section references prior qualitative research from college women in the U.S. and adolescents in Sweden but does not specify the number of studies, sample characteristics, or methodological details of the present research.
